    {
      "sentence": "The patient has profound hypotension and cold, clammy skin, with decreased cardiac output and high pulmonary capillary wedge pressure.",
      "grounding": "question",
      "question_quote": "decreased cardiac output and high pulmonary capillary wedge pressure",
      "passage_ids": []
    },
    {
      "sentence": "Low output despite elevated left-sided filling pressure points to cardiogenic shock.",
      "grounding": "none",
      "question_quote": null,
      "passage_ids": []
    },
    {
      "sentence": "Myocardial infarction, tachyarrhythmias, and severe aortic stenosis can all reduce cardiac output.",
      "grounding": "passages",
      "question_quote": null,
      "passage_ids": ["Neurology_Adams:002191"]
    },
    {
      "sentence": "Acute myocardial infarction can impair contraction, rapid atrial fibrillation can impair ventricular filling, and severe valvular stenosis can limit forward flow, so I, II, and IV are the best combination.",
      "grounding": "none",
      "question_quote": null,
      "passage_ids": []
    },
    {
      "sentence": "Massive pulmonary embolism can also lower cardiac output, but it classically causes obstructive shock without elevated wedge pressure; hemorrhage and sepsis classically cause hypovolemic and distributive shock, respectively.",
